READS_AT_1X.notes: Recoloured foliage median luminance dropped ~79 vs main ~94-105 (lawn ~130); share of foliage pixels at/above near-grass value (L>=115) halved (canopy 36%->20%, tool-village 33%->17%, village50 37%->18%); hue moved from ~116deg to ~126deg (bluer than lawn ~90deg). At 1x all forest blobs in after-canopy-1x, the west forest in after-tool-village-1x (0-140,455-720) and tree rows in river-town/village50/facilities separate clearly from the lawn; visibly better than main-*. Weakest spots: olive/yellow-green deciduous clumps on canopy edges (after-canopy-1x ~(210,230), (40,270)) are still the closest to lawn value but remain outlined and darker.

STYLE_MATCH.notes: Same pixel language and outline; no black blobs or neon. Trees keep lit upper tier and dark lower/shadow tiers (tree-art palette 148,179,83 flecks / 73,127,60 lit / 41,101,53 / 16,76,47 / 6,51,40 shadow). Warm variant in village50 keeps hue ~98deg (unchanged from main), only value lowered, still reads olive/warm vs the plain teal-green trees (see village50 top-left row). Mild note: hand-drawn oakA/oakB in after-tree-art-3x read somewhat cooler/teal and the lit tone dominates, so clump tiers are softer than in the canopy autotile, but still distinct.

NO_SEAMS.notes: Neighbour-pixel jump across 16px grid lines inside changed foliage is not higher than off-grid (canopy after 43.0 grid vs 52.5 off-grid; tool-village 52.3 vs 49.1, main 61.8 vs 56.8 - same ratio). No 16px cell in canopy-1x/tool-village/river-town/village50 retains old bright foliage colours (only 6 stray pixels in canopy-1x, near-black/outline tones at cells (416,288),(176,208),(80,304)); unchanged old colours are only near-black outlines (12,34,34 etc.). Pre-existing (identical in main): rectangular darker/lighter forest-floor grass patches with hard 16px edges under canopy borders (after-canopy-1x around forest bottoms e.g. (180-330,250-300), (390-480,290-305); after-tool-village-1x dark floor (0-140,455-720) and light patch (300-415,0-160)); dark teal gaps between trees in canopy interior.
